subject: Physics
unitTitle: Application of Physics in Other Fields

questions.question: Which fundamental sub-field of physics provides the atomic theory and quantum mechanical principles that ultimately explain chemical bonding and molecular structure?

options.text: Fluid Dynamics
Atomic and Subatomic Physics
Geometrical Optics
Classical Thermodynamics

questions.explanation: Atomic and subatomic particle physics explains the rules governing electrons and atomic nuclei, forming the theoretical foundation for chemical bonds and molecular behavior studied in chemistry.

questions.question: Human speech is generated when exhaled air from the lungs passes through the vocal cords in the larynx, causing them to vibrate. How is this sound transmitted to the eardrum of a listener?

options.text: As transverse electromagnetic waves through a vacuum
As mechanical longitudinal waves causing pressure variations in air molecules
As static electrical charges moving along nerve fibers
As gravitational ripples propagating through the atmosphere

questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical longitudinal wave. Vibrating vocal cords disturb surrounding air molecules, producing propagating compressions and rarefactions that cause the listener's eardrum to vibrate.

questions.question: Civil engineering relies heavily on Newtonian mechanics to ensure structural safety. Which branch of mechanics specifically deals with forces acting on stationary structures like bridges and skyscrapers to keep them in equilibrium?

options.text: Hydrodynamics
Statics
Quantum Electrodynamics
Aerodynamics

questions.explanation: Statics is the sub-discipline of mechanics focused on analyzing forces and torques acting on rigid bodies in static equilibrium, ensuring structures like bridges and buildings remain stable without collapsing.

questions.question: Conventional X-ray radiography produces shadow images of internal human body structures primarily because X-rays:

options.text: Are strongly absorbed by dense structures like bone, while passing more easily through soft tissues
Are reflected completely by muscle tissue back to the detector
Emit visible light that illuminates internal body cavities
Excite water molecules to emit high-frequency radio signals

questions.explanation: High-density tissues containing heavier elements (such as calcium in bones) absorb X-ray photons significantly more than softer tissues, creating contrasting shadow images on detectors.

questions.question: What type of electromagnetic waves are primarily used in RADAR systems to detect the distance, speed, and position of aircraft?

options.text: Gamma rays
Ultraviolet rays
Radio waves and microwaves
Visible blue light

questions.explanation: RADAR (Radio Detection and Ranging) utilizes radio waves or microwaves transmitted into space, which bounce off target objects (like aircraft) and return to a receiver to determine location and speed.

questions.question: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) relies on which fundamental physical property of hydrogen nuclei (protons) in human tissue when exposed to a strong external magnetic field and radiofrequency pulses?

options.text: The thermal expansion coefficient of cellular fluid
Nuclear magnetic spin and resonance absorption/emission of radiofrequency energy
The speed of sound waves reflecting off dense bones
Ionization of cellular atoms leading to electrical discharges

questions.explanation: Protons in hydrogen atoms (abundant in tissue water) possess magnetic spin alignment in a strong magnetic field. When radiofrequency pulses match their Larmor frequency, protons resonate and emit detectable RF signals as they relax.

questions.question: Astronomers determine the chemical composition of distant stars and interstellar gas clouds without physical sampling primarily by analyzing:

options.text: The total gravitational pull exerted by the star on Earth
Emission and absorption line spectra in the star's electromagnetic radiation
The seismic wave velocities recorded by terrestrial seismographs
The mechanical pressure of solar wind particles hitting upper atmosphere

questions.explanation: According to atomic physics (Bohr model), electrons make discrete energy transitions emitting or absorbing light at specific characteristic wavelengths, creating unique spectral signatures for each element.

questions.question: Geophysicists study the deep interior structure of the Earth (such as differentiating the liquid outer core from the solid inner core) using which physical technique?

options.text: Measuring the reflection and refraction of seismic body waves (P-waves and S-waves) generated by earthquakes
Direct optical observation using deep infrared lasers
Measuring atmospheric temperature variations during volcanic eruptions
Tracking electrostatic charge build-up on the surface of tectonic plates

questions.explanation: Seismic waves travel through Earth's interior. Primary (P) longitudinal waves pass through solids and liquids, whereas secondary (S) transverse waves cannot propagate through liquid media, revealing Earth's layered internal structure.

questions.question: How does Computed Tomography (CT scan) differ fundamentally from a standard two-dimensional planar X-ray radiography image?

options.text: CT scans use magnetic fields instead of ionizing radiation.
CT scans combine multiple X-ray projections taken from a rotating ring of detectors using computer algorithms to reconstruct 3D cross-sectional slice images.
CT scans measure high-frequency ultrasound reflections rather than electromagnetic rays.
CT scans inject radioactive gamma emitters to track cellular metabolism.

questions.explanation: Unlike flat 2D X-rays, a CT scanner rotates an X-ray source and detectors around the patient to take multiple cross-sectional attenuation profiles, which a computer processes into detailed 3D tomographic slices.

questions.question: Optical fiber cables transmit huge volumes of digital data across global telecommunication networks at high speeds using light pulses. What core optical principle ensures light remains trapped inside the fiber core without escaping?

options.text: Diffuse reflection from outer metallic shielding
Total internal reflection at the boundary between the core and cladding with a lower refractive index
Complete absorption of light waves by surrounding insulation
Polarization of visible light by magnetic fields

questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs when light traveling through an optically denser core strikes the interface with lower-index cladding at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle, preventing light loss.

questions.question: Thermal imaging devices used in military night-vision technology operate by detecting infrared radiation. What physical law dictates that all objects with a temperature above absolute zero emit thermal electromagnetic radiation?

options.text: Bernoulli's principle
Stefan-Boltzmann law of blackbody radiation
Coulomb's law of electrostatics
Faraday's law of induction

questions.explanation: Every object above 0 K emits thermal radiation due to thermal motion of charged particles. The Stefan-Boltzmann and Planck blackbody laws relate an object's temperature to the intensity and spectrum of emitted infrared light.

questions.question: A defense radar system emits a high-frequency microwave pulse toward an approaching aircraft. The echo pulse reflected from the aircraft is received by the radar antenna exactly 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ seconds after transmission. Taking the speed of electromagnetic waves in air as c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s, what is the distance R from the radar station to the aircraft?

options.text: 15 km
30 km
60 km
300 km

questions.explanation: The total round-trip distance traveled by the pulse is 2R = c × t. Thus, the target distance R = (c × t) / 2 = (3.0 × 10⁸ m/s × 2.0 × 10⁻⁴ s) / 2 = (6.0 × 10⁴ m) / 2 = 3.0 × 10⁴ m = 30 km.

questions.question: Doppler ultrasound imaging is widely used in cardiovascular diagnostics to measure blood flow velocity in arteries. If blood flows toward an ultrasound transducer emitting sound of frequency f₀, how is the detected frequency f' of the reflected echo shifted relative to f₀?

options.text: f' is equal to f₀ because sound speed remains constant in blood.
f' is higher than f₀ (positive Doppler shift) because moving blood cells act as approaching sound reflectors.
f' is lower than f₀ (negative Doppler shift) due to viscous attenuation.
f' drops to zero because blood completely absorbs ultrasound energy.

questions.explanation: According to the Doppler effect, when a wave reflects off a target moving toward the transducer (like approaching blood cells), the reflected frequency f' is shifted upward (f' > f₀). The magnitude of the shift is directly proportional to blood flow velocity.

questions.question: A ballistic missile operates in two distinct flight phases: a powered initial launch phase driven by rocket motors, followed by an unpowered exoatmospheric phase. Which physical laws govern the trajectory of the missile during its unpowered ballistic phase and its directional maneuverability in space?

options.text: Hydrostatic buoyancy laws and Archimedes' principle
Newtonian mechanics (gravitational free fall) for trajectory, and conservation of momentum (rocket thrust ejection) for maneuverability
Ohm's law and magnetic levitation
Snell's law of optical refraction and wave interference

questions.explanation: During the unpowered phase, the missile moves along an elliptical trajectory governed by Newton's law of gravitation (free fall). Course adjustments in space rely on Newton's third law and conservation of momentum via directional gas exhaust thrust.

questions.question: In modern radiation therapy for cancer treatment (Linear Accelerator / LINAC), high-energy Megavoltage X-rays or gamma rays are directed at tumor tissues. How do these ionizing radiations selectively destroy cancerous cells at the cellular level?

options.text: By heating cellular water to 100 °C to cause mechanical boiling
By direct and indirect ionization that breaks single- and double-strand DNA bonds, preventing uninhibited malignant cell replication
By magnetizing blood hemoglobin to stop local circulation
By freezing cellular membranes through thermal conduction

questions.explanation: High-energy ionizing radiation ejects electrons from biological atoms, creating free radicals and directly severing single- and double-strand DNA chemical bonds. Tumor cells, which divide rapidly and lack efficient repair mechanisms, undergo apoptosis.
